svg.title: The deriver: one call per batch
svg.desc: Top: session 1 as the deriver sees it, three messages, each in a tag with its index, its peer, whether that peer is the one being modelled, and its time. One model call, 923 tokens in, returns six explicit conclusions, each with Anton as the subject and the time of the batch's last message: planning a dinner in Berlin for the week of March 21, 2026; a strict vegetarian diet for eight years; a severe, anaphylactic peanut allergy; Indian cuisine; paneer dishes; a budget of about 40 euros per person. Bottom: the three rules for saving. An exact duplicate (same text, level and, for explicit rows, session) is dropped and the existing row counted again. A near duplicate (cosine distance 0.05 or less, same level and, for explicit rows, same session) is merged, and the richer text wins. Otherwise the row is stored. So the peanut allergy said in March and again in July is stored twice.
svg.text: The deriver: one call per batch
The deriver sees the new messages and nothing else: no stored conclusions, no earlier session. Saving then drops or
session 1, as it appears in the prompt
I'm planning a dinner for my sister's visit to Berlin next week. Worth saying up front: I've been strictly vegetarian for eight years, and I have a
severe peanut allergy — anaphylactic, not a preference.
Understood — no meat, and peanuts are a hard exclusion. Any cuisine you lean towards?
Indian, usually. Paneer dishes especially. And I'd rather not spend more than about 40 euros a head.
Explicit facts about the target peer, one each, with
six explicit rows, each stamped 2026-03-14 12:02, the time of the batch's last message
Anton is planning a dinner in Berlin for the
Anton has followed a strict vegetarian diet
Anton has a severe, anaphylactic peanut
Anton has a budget of approximately 40
euros per person for the dinner.
an exact duplicate (same text, level, and for explicit rows session) is dropped; the stored row is counted again
a near duplicate (cosine distance ≤ 0.05, same level, and for explicit rows same session) is merged: the richer text wins
March: “a severe, anaphylactic peanut allergy” · July: “a peanut allergy” · different sessions, so both stored
From the first run of a Honcho 3.3.0 server on the example
